title: Ozone and nitrogen dioxide through a summer day

stimulus.title: Hourly NO2 and ozone at a city monitor on a clear July weekday and a cloudy July weekday

table.caption: Hourly average concentrations in parts per billion (ppb) at one city monitor (invented data for practice)

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Identify the time when NO2 peaks on the clear day and the time when ozone peaks on the clear day. Describe how the timing of the two peaks differs.

rubric.point: Identifies the NO2 peak at 8 a.m. (68 ppb) and the ozone peak at 2 p.m. (115 ppb).
accept: NO2 highest at 8 a.m.; ozone highest at 2 p.m.
NO2 peaks in the morning rush hour at 68 ppb and ozone peaks mid-afternoon at 115 ppb

rubric.point: Describes that the ozone peak comes about six hours after the NO2 peak.
accept: the ozone peak lags the NO2 peak by about six hours

parts.sample: On the clear day NO2 peaks at 8 a.m. at 68 ppb, and ozone peaks at 2 p.m. at 115 ppb. The ozone peak comes about six hours after the NO2 peak.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Calculate the percent change in ozone on the clear day from 8 a.m. to 2 p.m. Show your setup.

rubric.point: Correct setup: (115 - 18) / 18 × 100, with the difference in brackets and the old value (18) in the denominator.

parts.sample: Setup: (115 ppb - 18 ppb) / 18 ppb × 100. Answer: about 539%, an increase.

mistakes.why: Divide by the old value (the 8 a.m. reading, 18 ppb), not the new one.
Without brackets the division happens first. Write (115 - 18) / 18 × 100.
That is 115 as a percent of 18. Subtract first: (115 - 18) / 18 × 100.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Explain why ozone on the clear day rises after NO2 peaks, naming the role of sunlight.

rubric.point: Explains that sunlight splits NO2 into NO and a single oxygen atom.
accept: sunlight breaks NO2 apart to release an oxygen atom

rubric.point: Explains that the oxygen atom combines with O2 to form ozone, so ozone builds as NO2 is used up (VOCs keep NO from destroying it).
accept: the free oxygen atom joins oxygen gas to make ozone, which accumulates as VOCs tie up the NO

parts.sample: Morning traffic releases NO, which forms NO2 by about 8 a.m. As the sun gets stronger, sunlight splits NO2 into NO and a single oxygen atom. The oxygen atom joins an O2 molecule to form ozone. VOCs react with the NO so it does not break the ozone down, so ozone accumulates and peaks in the early afternoon while NO2 falls.

parts.label: d
parts.prompt: Make a claim about the effect of sunlight on ozone formation, and justify your claim with data from the table.

rubric.point: Claim: sunlight increases ozone formation (more sunlight, more ozone).
accept: ozone is higher on the sunny day

rubric.point: Justifies with paired values: at 2 p.m. ozone was 115 ppb on the clear day but 34 ppb on the cloudy day (or another correct comparison).
accept: 115 ppb clear versus 34 ppb cloudy at 2 p.m.
the clear-day peak is more than three times the cloudy-day peak

parts.sample: Sunlight increases ozone formation. At 2 p.m. ozone reached 115 ppb on the clear day but only 34 ppb on the cloudy day, when less sunlight reached the NO2.

parts.label: e
parts.prompt: Propose a solution, other than reducing car traffic, that a city could adopt to reduce ground-level ozone, and explain how it works.

rubric.point: Proposes a realistic city-level solution other than reducing traffic, such as a rule limiting VOCs in paints and solvents, vapor recovery nozzles at gas stations, or limits on NOx from power plants and factories.
accept: require vapor recovery nozzles at gas stations
limit VOC content in paints and solvents
cap NOx emissions from power plants

rubric.point: Explains how it works: it cuts a primary pollutant (VOCs or NOx) that reacts in sunlight to make ozone.
accept: fewer VOCs means NO is free to break ozone down, so less ozone builds up
less NOx means less NO2 for sunlight to split

parts.sample: The city could require vapor recovery nozzles at all gas stations. They capture gasoline vapor, a VOC, as tanks are filled. With fewer VOCs in the air, less NO is tied up, so more of the ozone is broken down and less ozone builds up on sunny afternoons.
